about: Every route the CMS maps, once. The workbench, the curl generator and the endpoint strip all read this file. A service test fails if a route is added, removed or opened to a different role without it being updated here.

areas.title: Events in
areas.blurb: How the CMS tells this service what changed.

areas.title: Operations
areas.blurb: Health, the queue and test-only tools.

endpoints.title: Send a batch of events
endpoints.what: The webhook. A JSON array of up to 500 events (publish, unPublish, delete). The batch is validated and stored in one transaction, then acknowledged; the worker applies it a moment later.

body.note: An array of events. Each has type, id, timestamp, and for publish/unPublish a version and a payload object. Delete needs only type, id and timestamp.

responses.202: Stored safely, not yet applied. Every accepted event shows outcome queued. Follow the Location header, or GET /cms/batches/{batchId}.
responses.200: Decided at once: every event was rejected or ignored (or the batch was empty), so nothing was queued.
responses.400: The body is not a JSON array, is not valid JSON, or is nested too deeply (the depth limit counts the whole request: the array, the event and the payload).
responses.401: No credentials, or wrong ones. Repeated wrong passwords from one address are throttled.
responses.403: Signed in, but not as the CMS account.
responses.413: Over 5 MiB, or more than 500 events. Nothing was stored. Declare Content-Length so this is answered before the body is read.
responses.429: The queue is full or too many batches are being read at once. Retry-After says when to try again; nothing was stored.
responses.503: The service could not store the batch. Nothing was kept; send it again.

endpoints.title: Follow a batch
endpoints.what: Where a batch has got to: queued, completed (with each event's final outcome) or failed. Never returns payloads.

params.name: batchId
params.about: The batchId from the acknowledgement of POST /cms/events.

responses.200: The batch and its per-event results. status is queued, completed or failed.

endpoints.title: List records
endpoints.what: Entities in id order, a page at a time by cursor. Users see published, enabled entities; admins see all of them, each with a status block.

query.name: limit
query.about: Page size, 1 to 100 (default 50). Out-of-range numbers are clamped; text is a 400.

query.name: cursor
query.about: The nextCursor from the previous page. Treat it as opaque.

responses.200: A page: items and nextCursor (null on the last page).
responses.400: The limit is not a whole number, or the cursor is not one this service produced.
responses.403: The CMS account cannot read the API.

endpoints.title: Read one record
endpoints.what: One entity with its payload, version, checksum and last-update time. A hidden entity looks exactly like a missing one.

responses.200: The entity. Admins also get a status block (published, disabled by).
responses.404: Missing, unpublished, disabled or deleted. For a user these are indistinguishable on purpose; ask as an admin to tell them apart.
responses.403: The CMS account cannot read the API.

endpoints.title: Disable a record
endpoints.what: Hide an entity from users without touching the CMS's own data. Audited.

responses.200: The new state: whether it is visible to users and who disabled it.

endpoints.title: Enable a record
endpoints.what: Undo a disable. The entity is visible again if the CMS has it published.

endpoints.title: Upload a small file
endpoints.what: One request, up to the simple limit (8 MiB by default). Streamed to disk into quarantine; it is not served until the scanner has cleared it.

params.name: key
params.about: A name for the file: 1 to 200 characters, no slash, backslash or control characters.

headers.name: Content-Type
headers.about: The declared type. The scanner checks it against what the bytes really are.

headers.name: X-Content-SHA256
headers.about: Optional. If sent, the upload is refused when the content does not hash to it.

body.note: The raw bytes. Choose a file, or generate some.

responses.202: Received and quarantined. The body has the asset id and state quarantined. Poll GET /cms/assets/{id} until it is clean.
responses.400: Bad key, bad checksum text, a checksum that does not match, or an empty body.
responses.413: Over the simple limit: use a multipart upload.
responses.429: The store is full. Nothing was kept.

endpoints.title: Start a multipart upload
endpoints.what: S3-style: say what you are going to send (key, type, total size) and get an upload id and the part limits back.

responses.201: Started. The body has uploadId, the minimum and maximum part size, the part limit and when it expires.
responses.400: Missing or invalid key or size, or the body is not the expected JSON.

endpoints.title: Upload one part
endpoints.what: One part of a multipart upload. Parts can be sent in parallel and sent again (the last one wins). Every part but the last must be at least the minimum size.

responses.200: Stored. The body has the part's size and SHA-256; keep it for the complete call.
responses.400: Part number out of range, checksum mismatch, or the parts add up to more than was declared.
responses.404: Unknown, expired, completed or aborted upload.
responses.413: A part is larger than the maximum part size.

endpoints.title: Complete a multipart upload
endpoints.what: List the parts in order. They are assembled, hashed and checked against the declared size, then quarantined for scanning.

body.note: parts: each part's number and SHA-256, in order, none missing.

responses.202: Assembled and quarantined. The body is the asset.
responses.400: A part is missing, out of order, has the wrong checksum, is too small, or the total is not the declared size.

endpoints.title: Abort a multipart upload
endpoints.what: Abandon an upload and remove its parts.

endpoints.title: Ask about an asset
endpoints.what: The asset's state (quarantined, clean, rejected, failed), checksum and scan verdict. Never the bytes.

responses.200: The asset. state tells you whether it can be served; verdict and signature say what the scanner found.
responses.404: No such asset (or it was deleted).
responses.403: Users cannot ask about assets, only download clean ones.

endpoints.title: Download an asset
endpoints.what: Streams a clean asset. Supports Range, If-Range, ETag and If-None-Match, so many ranges can be fetched in parallel and a download resumed. Always an attachment, never sniffed or framed.

headers.name: Range
headers.about: bytes=0-99 (first 100), bytes=-100 (last 100), bytes=100- (from 100). Other units are ignored.

headers.name: If-None-Match
headers.about: An ETag from an earlier download: 304 if unchanged.

responses.206: The range asked for, with Content-Range.
responses.304: Not modified since the ETag you sent.
responses.404: Missing, deleted, or not clean. A quarantined or rejected asset is the same 404 as one that never existed.
responses.416: The range starts beyond the end of the file.
responses.429: Too many downloads open at once for this caller.

endpoints.title: Check an asset without downloading
endpoints.what: The same answer as the download, without the bytes: size, type and ETag.

responses.200: Headers only: Content-Length, Content-Type, ETag, Accept-Ranges.

endpoints.title: Delete an asset for good
endpoints.what: Hard delete: the row goes and the bytes are overwritten and removed (best effort on SSDs). Audited.

endpoints.title: List assets
endpoints.what: Assets with their state, newest first, optionally one state only.

responses.400: state is not one of the four states.

endpoints.title: Re-scan an asset
endpoints.what: Put a clean asset back in quarantine for another scan (for example after the scanner's signatures were updated). It is not served again until cleared.

responses.409: Only a clean asset can be re-scanned (or it does not exist).

endpoints.title: Requeue a set-aside asset
endpoints.what: An asset whose scanning kept failing is set aside, still unserved. This tries it again.

responses.409: Only an asset whose scanning was set aside can be requeued (or it does not exist).

endpoints.title: Re-scan everything cleared by an older scanner
endpoints.what: Every clean asset records which scanner version cleared it. This queues the ones cleared by an older version.

responses.200: The scanner version and how many assets were queued.

endpoints.title: Is the queue keeping up?
endpoints.what: Batches and events waiting, the age of the oldest, space used and the failed batches (with their bytes).

endpoints.title: Requeue a failed batch
endpoints.what: Put a batch the worker set aside back in the queue, once the cause is fixed. Audited.

endpoints.title: Erase everything (test only)
endpoints.what: Erase every entity, tombstone, ledger row and queued batch. Needs the confirmation phrase. The route exists only when Admin:AllowReset is on, which is refused in Production. The audit log survives.

body.note: The confirmation phrase must be exactly this.

responses.200: Erased: the counts of what was removed.
responses.400: The confirmation phrase is missing or wrong.
responses.404: The route is switched off (the default).

endpoints.title: Is it up?
endpoints.what: Whether the service is running and its database reachable. No credentials needed.
